note: Programmes that fund a person or a company rather than employ them: accelerators, talent investors, founder fellowships, and equity-free grants. Cheque sizes and equity are recorded only where the programme publishes them; cohort dates are deliberately absent, because they move every year and a stale date presented as fact is worse than none. Every entry links to the page that actually governs it.

programmes.name: Y Combinator
programmes.gives: US$500,000: $125,000 on a post-money SAFE for 7%, plus $375,000 on an uncapped MFN SAFE
programmes.equity: 7% plus whatever the MFN SAFE converts into
programmes.format: In person in the Bay Area for the batch, then Demo Day
programmes.eligibility: Any team at any stage, including solo founders and students. No revenue or incorporation required to apply.
programmes.cycle: Batches run through the year, each with its own deadline; late applications are still read

programmes.name: Techstars Accelerator
programmes.gives: US$220,000 in most markets: $20,000 on a post-money convertible equity agreement plus $200,000 on an uncapped MFN SAFE (US$100,000 MFN in Asia-Pacific programmes)
programmes.equity: 5% in common stock, plus what the MFN SAFE later converts into
programmes.format: Mentor-driven, in person, one city and theme per programme
programmes.eligibility: Early-stage teams; each city programme sets its own focus, and some are sector or region specific
programmes.cycle: Programmes open on their own schedules across the year; the accelerator page lists which are accepting applications

programmes.name: Entrepreneur First
programmes.gives: An equity-free stipend while you find a co-founder and an idea, then investment in the company you form (up to US$250,000 on the US pathway: $125,000 for 8% plus $125,000 on an uncapped MFN SAFE)
programmes.equity: None while you are still forming; equity only in the company that results
programmes.format: Cohort of individuals, not companies — you arrive without a co-founder or an idea
programmes.duration: Around six months, form then build
programmes.eligibility: Individuals, including new graduates and researchers, who want to found rather than join. No team and no idea required.
programmes.cycle: Cohorts run a few times a year per city, each with its own deadline

programmes.name: Antler Residency
programmes.gives: A residency to find a co-founder and validate an idea, then pre-seed investment for teams the investment committee backs. Amounts and structure differ by location, and some locations charge a programme fee.
programmes.equity: Taken only from teams that are funded at the end of the residency; the percentage is location specific
programmes.format: Co-founder matching and validation sprint, then an internal investment committee
programmes.duration: Roughly two months to the investment decision
programmes.eligibility: Individuals and pairs, from new graduates to experienced operators; the London residency runs several times a year
programmes.cycle: Residencies start several times a year per city — check the location page for the next cohort and its terms

programmes.name: Conception X
programmes.gives: A fully funded nine-month deep-tech venture programme alongside your PhD, with training, coaching and investor access; participants can go on to raise through partner investors and the programme's angel syndicate
programmes.equity: None — the programme takes no equity and charges no fees
programmes.format: Part time alongside the doctorate, cohort based, UK-wide
programmes.eligibility: STEM PhD students in the UK who want to build a company from their research
programmes.cycle: One cohort a year, applications usually in the summer

programmes.name: Creator Fund
programmes.gives: Pre-seed investment in companies coming out of European universities, sourced by student and PhD investors on campus
programmes.equity: Equity investment on standard pre-seed terms
programmes.format: A fund rather than a programme: you pitch, there is no cohort
programmes.eligibility: Founders who are students, PhD researchers, or recent alumni of European universities, typically in deep tech, AI, life sciences, robotics and quantum
programmes.cycle: Open to approaches all year

programmes.name: Thiel Fellowship
programmes.gives: US$200,000 over two years, plus the foundation's network
programmes.equity: None — it is a grant
programmes.format: You leave or pause university for the duration
locations: Anywhere, with a pull toward the Bay Area
programmes.eligibility: Under 23 at the time of application, and willing to step away from a degree to build
programmes.cycle: Applications open annually

programmes.name: Z Fellows
programmes.gives: US$10,000 investment and a week-long programme with founders and investors
programmes.format: One intensive week, then ongoing network access
programmes.eligibility: Very early founders, including students and people who have not started yet
programmes.cycle: Cohorts run frequently through the year

programmes.name: Neo Scholars
programmes.gives: A scholarship, mentorship from senior engineers and founders, and access to Neo's community and later funding
programmes.equity: None for the scholarship itself
programmes.format: Selected from a technical challenge and interviews
programmes.eligibility: Computer science and engineering students in the US, typically undergraduates
programmes.cycle: One cohort a year, applications usually in the autumn

programmes.name: Emergent Ventures
programmes.gives: Grants and fellowships for projects, research and companies with an unusual upside; amounts are set case by case
programmes.equity: None — it is a grant
programmes.format: A short written application, no cohort
programmes.eligibility: Anyone with a project that is ambitious and hard to fund elsewhere, including students and researchers
programmes.cycle: Rolling, decided in batches

programmes.name: Innovate UK Young Innovators
programmes.gives: A grant plus a living allowance and a year of coaching; the amounts are set for each round
programmes.equity: None — it is a grant
programmes.format: Award plus structured support from a business coach
programmes.eligibility: UK residents aged 18 to 30 with a business idea with social or economic impact
programmes.cycle: Usually one round a year, opening in the summer

programmes.name: Enterprise Fellowships
programmes.gives: A grant to commercialise engineering research, plus training and mentoring
programmes.equity: None
programmes.format: Fellowship held at your institution while you spin the work out
programmes.eligibility: UK-based researchers, typically postdocs and late-stage PhDs, commercialising their own engineering research
programmes.cycle: Rounds open annually

programmes.name: Start Up Loans
programmes.gives: A government-backed personal loan for business purposes, with free mentoring
programmes.equity: None — it is a loan, repaid with interest
programmes.format: Application with a business plan and cash-flow forecast
programmes.duration: Repaid over one to five years
programmes.eligibility: UK residents aged 18 or over, trading for less than three years
programmes.cycle: Open all year

programmes.name: Google for Startups Accelerator
programmes.gives: Mentoring, technical support from Google engineers, and cloud credits
programmes.equity: None — Google takes no equity
programmes.format: Cohorts by region and by theme, such as AI or climate
programmes.eligibility: Startups with a product in market, usually seed to Series A; each cohort states its own bar
programmes.cycle: Cohorts open regularly by region and theme

programmes.name: NVIDIA Inception
programmes.gives: Hardware and software discounts, technical training, go-to-market support and investor introductions
programmes.equity: None — it is free to join
programmes.format: Membership programme rather than a cohort
programmes.eligibility: Any incorporated startup building in AI, data science, robotics or graphics
programmes.cycle: Open all year

programmes.name: Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub
programmes.gives: Azure and OpenAI credits, developer tooling, and technical support
programmes.equity: None
programmes.format: Self-serve membership with tiers as you grow
programmes.eligibility: Anyone building a startup, including pre-incorporation
programmes.cycle: Open all year

programmes.name: AWS Activate
programmes.gives: AWS credits, technical support and training
programmes.equity: None
programmes.format: Self-serve, with larger credit tiers through partner accelerators and VCs
programmes.duration: Credits valid for a fixed window
programmes.eligibility: Early-stage startups; the largest tiers require an affiliated accelerator or investor
programmes.cycle: Open all year

programmes.name: Founder Fellowship
programmes.gives: Funding and a community for people at the stage before an idea; terms are published on the fellowship page
programmes.equity: Taken on investment, see the page for current terms
programmes.format: Community-first, deliberately pre-idea
programmes.eligibility: Experienced builders and researchers leaving a role to figure out what to start
programmes.cycle: Cohorts a few times a year

programmes.name: Speedrun
programmes.gives: Investment and an intensive programme for companies at the intersection of technology and entertainment, including AI and games; the cheque and terms are published per batch
programmes.equity: See the current batch's published terms
programmes.format: In person in Los Angeles for the programme
programmes.eligibility: Teams building in games, AI, consumer and adjacent areas; very early is explicitly welcome
programmes.cycle: Batches open a few times a year

programmes.name: HF0 Residency
programmes.gives: A live-in residency for repeat founders, with investment on terms published by the programme
programmes.equity: See the residency page
programmes.format: Residential, in person, monastic by design
programmes.eligibility: Technical founders, weighted heavily toward people who have shipped before
programmes.cycle: Cohorts a few times a year

programmes.name: Founders Factory
programmes.gives: Investment plus hands-on product, design and growth teams; also runs a venture studio that builds from scratch with founders
programmes.equity: Taken in exchange for investment and the operating support
programmes.format: Accelerator and studio tracks, often with a corporate partner behind a sector
programmes.eligibility: Early-stage teams, with sector tracks that change as partners change
programmes.cycle: Rolling, by track

programmes.name: Deep Science Ventures
programmes.gives: A salaried venture creation programme in which scientists build a company around a chosen problem, with the studio co-founding alongside
programmes.equity: The studio co-founds and holds equity in what is created
programmes.format: Venture creation cohorts by sector — computation, climate, pharma, agriculture
programmes.duration: Around six months to company formation
programmes.eligibility: PhD-level scientists and engineers willing to found rather than research
programmes.cycle: Cohorts open once or twice a year by sector
